ImageContent.Description: Off the coast of Kvaløya in Troms, Northern Norway, humpback whales move through the cold Arctic waters in search of a proper feast. They visit this region during the winter months, following migrating herring into the fjords. Humpbacks are famous for bubble-net feeding, a remarkable hunting technique in which whales blow rings of bubbles to corral fish before lunging upwards, open-mouthed, to catch their prey. In today's image, a humpback slips beneath the icy waves under a glowing pastel sky, capturing a moment of tranquility in Norway's wild north.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Diving humpback whale, Kvaloya, Troms, Northern Norway

ImageContent.Description: Step into this peaceful redwood forest in Victoria, Australia, and the outside world can suddenly feel very far away. Coast redwoods (Sequoia sempervirens) tower overhead, forming a leafy canopy above the forest floor. These impressive trees have grown into one of the region's most distinctive woodland sights. With their tall trunks, deep green foliage and tranquil surroundings, the redwoods create an inviting place to wander, slow down and enjoy the quiet beauty of the forest.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Coast redwoods near Melbourne, Victoria, Australia

ImageContent.Description: These barn owls, bathed in evening light, are waiting for the hunt to begin. As night falls, these birds of prey swoop into action, listening for tiny movements in grass or leaves made by mice and voles. Their heart-shaped faces help funnel sound into some of the sharpest ears in the animal kingdom. This allows them to locate their prey with pinpoint precision in the dark before swooping silently, their soft feathers muffling their approach. In autumn, young barn owls strike out to find their own territories. As the nights grow longer, you might spot them earlier in the evening, gliding over fields in search of supper.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Pair of barn owls

ImageContent.Description: Sometimes, the best way to clear your head is to step outside. Today's image features the Trail of the Cedars, part of more than 1,100 kilometres of hiking trails in Glacier National Park, Montana, in the northwestern USA. Its 1.4-kilometre loop includes a raised boardwalk that cuts a path through western red cedar and hemlock trees. The park boasts routes for all abilities, taking in alpine lakes, wildflower meadows, mountain passes and wilderness stretching to the Canadian border.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Trail of the Cedars, Glacier National Park, Montana, USA

ImageContent.Description: Incredible views and rock-solid foundations are part of the charm of these ancient dwellings, set into the cliffside in New Mexico, USA. Nomads had long used the natural caves above Cliff Dweller Creek as temporary shelter, but it was the Native American Mogollon people who made them their home. Archaeologists believe they created dozens of rooms inside five alcoves in the 1270s and 1280s. Up to 15 families lived here at any one time, raising children, making pottery and overlooking the fertile Gila River valley where they grew crops and hunted wildlife. For reasons unknown, the Mogollon people moved on around 1300, leaving behind one of the American Southwest's most important archaeological sites.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument, New Mexico, USA

ImageContent.Description: As colder weather sets in, ice crystals form on the leaves of evergreen shrubs, like this azalea. Long gone are the pinks, orange and yellows of their spring blooms, but a new colourful display awaits, as their green leaves turn shades of red and purple. For the plants, the new pigments protect their leaves as temperatures drop, but for gardeners, they create a vibrant autumnal display, framed in white frost. When spring arrives, new growth will restore the shrub's green leaves, and the colourful cycle begins anew.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Frozen azalea with red leaves

ImageContent.Description: Welcome to Hong Kong, home to the world's largest collection of skyscrapers. Those pictured here tower above Victoria Harbour, whose deep waters allowed the island to develop as a busy trading port. Ships carrying tea, silk and other goods have passed through since the 1840s, but growth rocketed in the decades after World War II, fueling a construction boom. With little flat land available between the harbour and the hills, developers had to build upwards, creating this distinctive skyline. In 2026, Hong Kong has 569 buildings at least 150 metres tall high — more than any other city.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Victoria Harbour, Hong Kong, China

ImageContent.Description: Hidden within an ancient sandstone landscape, Face Canyon is one of 96 canyons stretching out from Lake Powell in the US state of Utah. Many are far from roads and would be hard to reach if they hadn't been flooded by the lake, created in 1963 during the construction of the Glen Canyon Dam. The lake's waters back up nearly 300 kilometres, along creeks and canyons which you can explore by boat, kayak or personal watercraft.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Butte at sunset, Face Canyon, Lake Powell, Utah, USA

ImageContent.Description: Water, sunlight and lush greenery come together at Rainbow Falls in Hilo, on Hawaii's Big Island. Here, the Wailuku River plunges  24 metres over a lava ledge, sending mist into the air as it reaches the pool below. On sunny mornings, that mist can catch the light and produce the colourful rainbows that gave the falls their name.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Rainbow Falls on the Wailuku River, Hilo, Hawaii, USA

ImageContent.Description: Snow transforms Utah's Bryce Canyon National Park, blanketing the landscape in white while its fiery orange-red hoodoos rise above the snowy terrain. Seen from Sunset Point, one of the park's most famous overlooks, these fantastical shapes are part of the Claron Formation, whose limestone was deposited about 50 million years ago and later shaped by weathering and erosion. Because much of the park rises above 2,440 metres, snow can arrive as early as October. In today's image, snow clings to the canyon's ridges and spires while mist drifts across the cliffs, creating an iconic winter scene in the American Southwest.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Sunset Point, Bryce Canyon National Park, Utah, USA

ImageContent.Description: As Britain's only native squirrel species, red squirrels thrive in Scotland's Cairngorms National Park. An important refuge, the park offers ancient Caledonian pine forests and newer conifer woodlands, with plentiful habitat and food for squirrels foraging for Scots pine seeds, nuts and other tasty morsels year-round. In today's image, a red squirrel is perched amid warm orange and yellow leaves, looking right at home as it ponders its next move in the Scottish Highlands.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Red squirrel in Cairngorms National Park, Highlands, Scotland

ImageContent.Description: Today's image shows the gradual coiling of a young fiddlehead's tip, echoing the geometric patterns seen throughout nature. In mathematics, the Fibonacci sequence follows a similar progression, each number formed by adding the two before it: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and so on. Eventually the young fern frond shown here will unfurl as it grows, but elsewhere in the plant world, the sequence will continue to appear in the spiralling arrangements of sunflower heads, pinecones, succulents and pineapples.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Fiddlehead fern

ImageContent.Description: Off Greenland's west coast, enormous icebergs drift through the cold waters, creating a landscape that's constantly changing. Many originate from the nearby Jakobshavn Glacier, one of the world's fastest and most active glaciers. The surrounding Ilulissat Icefjord, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, lies about 250 kilometres north of the Arctic Circle. Here, towering blocks of ice break away and begin their slow journey towards the open sea, forming one of Greenland's most remarkable natural sights.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Icebergs, Ilulissat, Greenland

ImageContent.Description: Bathed in a sun-kissed glow, Nice is a patchwork of terracotta rooftops, historic churches and pastel façades along the French Riviera, as seen in today's image. Founded by ancient Greeks and long connected to the Italian royal House of Savoy, Nice officially became part of France in 1860. Today, that layered past remains visible throughout the coastal city in the south of France, where old-world architecture meets the blue Mediterranean waters and sunlit hills of the Côte d'Azur.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Nice, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
